title: Uniforms & helmets
about: Soldiers date a photo almost to the war: helmet shapes changed with each conflict and camouflage patterns changed every 10–20 years. Years are when the item was standard issue; reservists and other armies often kept them longer.

items.tell: Spiked leather helmet; replaced in the trenches by the Stahlhelm from 1916
Shallow 'soup bowl' with a wide brim: WW1 Tommies, still used in WW2
Crest ridge on top, peaks front and back, badge on the front
'Coal scuttle' with flared neck guard: WW1 (from 1916) and WW2
Round Soviet steel helmet with a small rim, used for 50 years
Round steel pot, often with net or cloth cover: WW2, Korea, Vietnam

items.w: Personnel Armor System for Ground Troops
items.tell: Kevlar 'Fritz' with a lip over the ears and neck: Grenada to early Iraq
Smaller cut, no brim, night-vision mount on the front, pads inside
Pointed cloth helmet with a big red star: Russian Civil War and 1920s–30s
Soft wide-brim jungle hat, first in Vietnam
Sharp-edged 'splinter' shapes with rain streaks: Wehrmacht smocks and tent sheets
Horizontal black brush strokes on green and brown
Green and brown leaf shapes with black branches: late Vietnam
British brush-stroke woodland camo, replaced by MTP around 2010
Large green, brown, black and sand blobs: 1980s–2000s US troops
Sand with brown blobs and black-and-white 'chips': Gulf War 1991
Plain sand, tan and brown: Somalia, Afghanistan 2001, Iraq 2003
Dense small dots of green, brown and black
Pixelated digital woodland or desert

items.army: US Army (as OCP from 2015), UK (MTP), Australia
items.tell: Soft blended tan, green and brown: Afghanistan 2010+
Grey-green pixels: US Army in Iraq/Afghanistan 2005–2014
